newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.84 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.84 pct to new record.

text.p: Shares on Istanbul's stock exchange gained an average 1.84 percent in a continued rally on Monday despite profit-taking which erased part of the early gains, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at a new all-time high of 1,054, up 19 points from Friday's previous record of 1,035.In dollar terms, it stood at 96.3 cents, up from Friday's 95.5 cents and compared to a 1996 record of $1 on April 8.
It had surged six percent on Thursday and Friday after the new year holiday from December 27 to January 2.
Trade volume leapt to 17.93 trillion lira ($163.7 million) from Friday's 13.79 trillion ($127.3 million).
Brokers said lower money and bond rates and 1996 profit prospects of companies continued to buoy demand.
"A rise was expected at the beginning of 1997. The trend remains upward, with intermittent profit-taking and $1 is the initial target," said Turgay Ozaner from Global securities.
"Lower repo rates (in the bond market), a quiet dollar and both 1996 and (1997) first quarter profit expectations in companies is fuelling demand. There is cash influx to the market," he said.
